courseTitle: Stone Age to Iron Age Britain (c. 800,000 BC–AD 43)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: Stone Age to Iron Age
root.gloss: How life in Britain changed from Ice Age mammoth hunters and sunken Doggerland to Neolithic farms, Stonehenge, Bronze Age smiths, and Iron Age hillforts.

children.label: 1. Hunters to First Farmers
children.gloss: Old and Middle Stone Age hunter-gatherers survived the Ice Age and flooded Doggerland before New Stone Age boat travellers brought Britain’s first farms and Skara Brae.

children.label: 1. Ice Age & Sunken Doggerland
children.q2Chain: Ice Age mammoth caves & flint handaxes → Warming Mesolithic forests at Star Carr → Rising seas flood Doggerland (c. 6500 BC)
children.gloss: Ice Age mammoth caves & flint handaxes → Warming Mesolithic forests at Star Carr → Rising seas flood Doggerland (c. 6500 BC)

children.label: Ice Age Caves & Flint Handaxes
children.gloss: Old Stone Age families walked mud at Happisburgh, sheltered in limestone caves, and chipped sharp flint handaxes to hunt woolly mammoths.

children.label: Ice Snow & Zero Metal Tools
children.gloss: Thick snow covered northern Britain; Families sheltered inside Creswell Crags.

children.label: Knapped Flint & Mammoth Hunts
children.gloss: Barefoot footprints left at Happisburgh; Chipped tear-drop flint handaxes.

children.label: → Ice Melted Into Green Forests
children.gloss: Mammoths gave meat, hides, bones; Warming weather ended Ice Age.

children.label: Cheddar Man & Star Carr Camps
children.gloss: As green forests spread in the Middle Stone Age, seasonal hunter-gatherers fished lakes, built wooden platforms at Star Carr, and carved antler headdresses.

children.label: Warming Woods Brought New Game
children.gloss: Red deer roamed green forests; Wild boar and hazelnuts thrived.

children.label: Cheddar Man & Antler Masks
children.gloss: Cheddar Man had blue eyes; Star Carr carved antler headdresses.

children.label: → Melting Ice Raised Sea Levels
children.gloss: Built wooden platforms by lakes; Moved seasonal camps along rivers.

children.label: Rising Waves Drown Doggerland
children.gloss: Around 6500 BC, water from melting northern ice sheets drowned the low green land bridge of Doggerland beneath the North Sea.

children.label: Melting Ice Poured Into Seas
children.gloss: Hunters once walked dry Doggerland; Speared eels and trapped beavers.

children.label: Storms Flooded Doggerland c. 6500 BC
children.gloss: Waves drowned low marshy plains; Trawlers still find mammoth teeth.

children.label: → Turned Britain Into an Island
children.gloss: Cut Britain off from Europe; Future newcomers arrived by boat.

children.label: 2. First Farmers & Skara Brae
children.q2Chain: Sea settlers bring wheat & sheep (c. 4000 BC) → Stone homes built at Skara Brae → Ancestor chambers raised at West Kennet
children.gloss: Sea settlers bring wheat & sheep (c. 4000 BC) → Stone homes built at Skara Brae → Ancestor chambers raised at West Kennet

children.label: First Crops, Sheep & Stone Axes
children.gloss: Wooden boats brought wheat, barley, sheep, and cattle across the sea around 4000 BC, starting New Stone Age farming in settled villages.

children.label: Boats Brought Seeds & Tame Herds
children.gloss: Brought tame sheep, pigs, cattle; Planted wheat and barley seeds.

children.label: Polished Axes & Clay Stew Pots
children.gloss: Polished stone axes felled forests; Flint sickles cut ripe stalks.

children.label: → Settled Villages Built All Year
children.gloss: Coiled clay bowls held stews; Steady harvests ended constant moving.

children.label: 1850 Storm Uncovers Skara Brae
children.gloss: A fierce winter storm in 1850 blew sand off Orkney to reveal eight snug stone Neolithic houses linked by roofed passages.

children.label: Windy Orkney Had Few Trees
children.gloss: Stacked flat coastal flagstones neatly; 1850 winter storm blew sand.

children.label: Stone Beds, Dressers & Drains
children.gloss: Eight homes linked by passages; Box beds, hearths, indoor drains.

children.label: → Rooted Villages Built Grand Tombs
children.gloss: Displayed treasures on stone dressers; Showed cosy settled village life.

children.label: West Kennet Long Barrow Tombs
children.gloss: Wiltshire farming families raised chalk mounds like West Kennet Long Barrow to honour nearly fifty ancestors inside dark stone chambers.

children.label: Five Chambers Under Chalk Mound
children.gloss: Heavy boulders guarded dark chambers; Held bones of fifty ancestors.

children.label: Clay Bowls & Hilltop Feasts
children.gloss: Left clay bowls and beads; Families feasted outside tomb entrance.

children.label: → Teamwork Prepared Stonehenge Next
children.gloss: Marked community claim to land; Proved villagers could move boulders.

children.label: 2. Stonehenge & Early Bronze
children.gloss: Neolithic communities hauled Welsh bluestones and 25-tonne sarsens to align Stonehenge with the sun before Beaker newcomers introduced copper, tin, and bronze.

children.label: 3. Secrets of Stonehenge
children.q2Chain: Antler-dug chalk henge & Welsh bluestones → 25-tonne sarsen trilithons & Durrington Walls → Heel Stone frames solstice sun
children.gloss: Antler-dug chalk henge & Welsh bluestones → 25-tonne sarsen trilithons & Durrington Walls → Heel Stone frames solstice sun

children.label: Chalk Henge & Welsh Bluestones
children.gloss: Workers dug a circular chalk ditch with red-deer antler picks around 3000 BC, then hauled eighty spotted bluestones 140 miles from Wales.

children.label: Antler Picks Dug Chalk Henge
children.gloss: Used cattle shoulder-bone shovels; Buried cremated ancestors inside bank.

children.label: 80 Bluestones Hauled 140 Miles
children.gloss: Quarried from Welsh Preseli Hills; Pulled on wooden sledges, ropes.

children.label: → Inspired Giant Sarsen Circle Next
children.gloss: United distant tribes in teamwork; Turned Salisbury Plain sacred.

children.label: 25-Tonne Sarsens & Feasts
children.gloss: Without wheels or cranes, builders dragged 25-tonne sarsen blocks on rollers, locked trilithon joints, and feasted at Durrington Walls.

children.label: 25-Tonne Blocks on Wood Rollers
children.gloss: Dragged sarsens twenty miles overland; Pounded smooth with stone balls.

children.label: Pegged Trilithons & Pork Feasts
children.gloss: Locked mortise-and-tenon stone joints; Roasted pigs at Durrington Walls.

children.label: → Angled Stones Toward Solstice Sky
children.gloss: Built warm chalk workers’ houses; Shaped horseshoe toward sun path.

children.label: Heel Stone & Solstice Sunbeams
children.gloss: Stonehenge lined up with the lone Heel Stone to frame the Midsummer sunrise and Midwinter sunset as a giant sky calendar.

children.label: Farmers Tracked Turning Seasons
children.gloss: Zero written records left behind; Archaeologists study buried sky clues.

children.label: Midsummer & Midwinter Sunbeams
children.gloss: Midsummer sun rose over Heel Stone; Midwinter sunset lit tallest trilithon.

children.label: Midsummer sun rose over Heel Stone
children.gloss: Midsummer sun rose over Heel Stone

children.label: Giant Solar Calendar & Shrine
children.gloss: Guided yearly planting and feasts; Soon met shiny Beaker metalwork.

children.label: 4. Bronze Age & Beaker People
children.q2Chain: Beaker newcomers & copper/tin mines (c. 2400 BC) → Casting tough liquid bronze axes → Gold capes & the Amesbury Archer
children.gloss: Beaker newcomers & copper/tin mines (c. 2400 BC) → Casting tough liquid bronze axes → Gold capes & the Amesbury Archer

children.label: Beaker Pots, Copper & Tin Mines
children.gloss: Beaker travellers sailed from Europe with bell-shaped pots and metalworking skills as miners dug Welsh copper and Cornish tin.

children.label: Beaker Folk Brought Metal Skills
children.gloss: Stamped comb patterns on beakers; Ended Britain’s long Stone Age.

children.label: Great Orme Copper & Cornish Tin
children.gloss: Crawled Great Orme copper tunnels; Smelted Cornish tin over fires.

children.label: → Smiths Mixed Harder Bronze Alloy
children.gloss: Crushed rock ran liquid metal; Supplied both metals for bronze.

children.label: Casting Tough Bronze Axes
children.gloss: Smiths mixed nine parts copper with one part tin and poured liquid bronze into reusable stone moulds for strong axes.

children.label: Pure Copper Bent Against Oak
children.gloss: Chipped flint snapped for good; Soft copper dented on trees.

children.label: Nine Parts Copper, One Part Tin
children.gloss: Poured liquid into two-piece moulds; Broken blades melted down again.

children.label: → Faster Farms & Rich Chiefs
children.gloss: Cleared thick woodland much faster; Enriched families on trade routes.

children.label: Gold Capes & Amesbury Archer
children.gloss: Dazzling gold capes and chemical tests on the Amesbury Archer’s teeth proved Bronze Age Britain had wealthy leaders linked to Europe.

children.label: Mold Gold Cape & Bush Barrow
children.gloss: Hammered thin sheets of gold; Wore crescent-moon lunulae collars.

children.label: Amesbury Archer’s 100+ Grave Goods
children.gloss: Five beakers, copper knives, gold; Tooth enamel proved Alpine childhood.

children.label: Proved Wide European Trade Links
children.gloss: Buried near Stonehenge c. 2300 BC; Linked British chiefs to Europe.

children.label: 3. Must Farm to Celtic Iron
children.gloss: Waterlogged mud at Must Farm preserved Britain’s oldest wheel and Bronze Age homes before Iron Age blacksmiths, Celtic hillforts, and Roman legions arrived.

children.label: 5. Must Farm: Britain’s Pompeii
children.q2Chain: Fire drops stilt houses into wet mud (c. 900 BC) → Porridge, cloth & oldest wheel saved → Dover sewn-plank boat crosses Channel
children.gloss: Fire drops stilt houses into wet mud (c. 900 BC) → Porridge, cloth & oldest wheel saved → Dover sewn-plank boat crosses Channel

children.label: Burning Stilts Seal in Wet Mud
children.gloss: Around 900 BC, a sudden fire dropped Must Farm’s oak stilt roundhouses into airless Cambridgeshire river mud near Flag Fen.

children.label: Oak Stilt Homes & Flag Fen Posts
children.gloss: Roundhouses stood over slow river; Timber causeway crossed Flag Fen.

children.label: Roof Fire Dropped Into Wet Mud
children.gloss: Families escaped sudden roof fire; Airless mud stopped wood rotting.

children.label: → Saved 3,000-Year Time Capsule
children.gloss: Nicknamed Must Farm Britain’s Pompeii; Sealed bowls, clothes, tools intact.

children.label: Porridge, Cloth & Oldest Wheel
children.gloss: Beneath Must Farm’s wet mud survived bowls of charred porridge with wooden spoons, woven plant cloth, eel traps, and a 1-metre wheel.

children.label: Charred Porridge & Eel Traps
children.gloss: Wooden spoon left inside bowl; Wove willow wicker eel traps.

children.label: 1-Metre Ash Wheel & Fine Cloth
children.gloss: Spun soft plant-fibre woven cloth; Oldest complete wheel in Britain.

children.label: Proved Skilled Farms & River Life
children.gloss: Bronze axes slotted in handles; Drove carts across nearby fields.

children.label: Sacred Waters & The Dover Boat
children.gloss: Mediterranean glass beads, Flag Fen water offerings, and the yew-stitched oak Dover Boat proved busy Channel sea trade.

children.label: Glass Beads & River Offerings
children.gloss: Mediterranean glass beads reached fens; Lowered bronze shields into water.

children.label: Oak Planks Stitched With Yew
children.gloss: Built before iron nails existed; Sealed oak seams with moss.

children.label: → Linked Britain & France by Sea
children.gloss: Paddled tin across English Channel; Spread new ideas toward Iron Age.

children.label: Spread new ideas toward Iron Age
children.gloss: Spread new ideas toward Iron Age

children.label: 6. Iron Age Celts & Hillforts
children.q2Chain: Iron ploughs & roundhouse harvests (c. 800 BC) → Rival tribes build Maiden Castle → Gold torcs, coins & AD 43 Roman invasion
children.gloss: Iron ploughs & roundhouse harvests (c. 800 BC) → Rival tribes build Maiden Castle → Gold torcs, coins & AD 43 Roman invasion

children.label: Iron Ploughs & Cosy Roundhouses
children.gloss: Blacksmiths hammered widespread British iron ore into tough ploughshares while families ground flour inside thatched roundhouses.

children.label: Reddish Iron Ore Lay Everywhere
children.gloss: Found across hills and bogs; Heated inside hot clay furnaces.

children.label: Ploughshares, Querns & Looms
children.gloss: Sliced heavy clay for wheat; Spun rotary querns inside roundhouses.

children.label: → Bumper Crops Grew Rival Tribes
children.gloss: Built warm wattle-and-daub walls; Wove bright wool on looms.

children.label: Celtic Tribes & Maiden Castle
children.gloss: Competing Celtic tribes ringed high ridges with steep ramparts at Maiden Castle and carved the chalk Uffington White Horse.

children.label: Growing Tribes Fought Over Land
children.gloss: Competed fiercely for prized cattle; Needed safe hilltop grain stores.

children.label: Maiden Castle Banks & Slingshots
children.gloss: Winding gates trapped raiding bands; Defenders hurled smooth slingshot stones.

children.label: → Guarded Markets & Chalk Art
children.gloss: Stored grain in underground pits; Carved chalk Uffington White Horse.

children.label: Gold Torcs, Coins & AD 43 Rome
children.gloss: Celtic smiths twisted gold torcs and minted stater coins before Emperor Claudius’s four Roman legions invaded in AD 43.

children.label: Druids & Snettisham Great Torc
children.gloss: Druids memorised sacred tribal laws; Twisted gold wire neck torcs.

children.label: Gold Stater Coins & Claudius AD 43
children.gloss: Stamped horses on gold staters; Claudius sent four Roman legions.

children.label: Ended Prehistory as Rome Arrived
children.gloss: Gifted horned helmets to Thames; Written history began in AD 43.
